mainTopic: Shoe status of the קב, the משנה of boys' קשרים, and healing practices and remedies on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a distinction: a support that only steadies a person's walk is not a shoe, but the קב of a קיטע carries his full weight, so it is treated like a shoe. רבי יוחנן uses this to correct a reciter's version of the משנה. Since a woman may do חליצה with the support, it may not be brought into the עזרה. The גמרא then gives three definitions of לוקטמין. A new משנה permits boys to go out on שבת with קשרים and princes with bells, and adds that really anyone may. The גמרא first explains the קשרים as madder bundles, but rejects this because a remedy would not be limited to young boys. It concludes that they are a shoe-strap tied on a boy who misses his father. This leads to a series of healing practices permitted on שבת from אבין בר הונא, a discussion of who said the swaddling ruling, and remedies אביי learned from the woman who raised him. These include the אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה against miscarriage, whose counterweight-of-a-counterweight question ends in תיקו, and three remedies for a one-day fever. The amud ends as a new statement of רב הונא begins.

steps.title: A steadying support versus a support you lean on
steps.stepSummary: The earlier item only helps a person walk straight. The קב of a קיטע carries his full weight, so it counts as a real shoe.
steps.simpleTranslation: [There] it is made only to steady his steps. Here, it is made to be leaned on, and he does lean his weight on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a contradiction. It explains why the wooden leg is treated differently from another support that seemed similar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is what each item is for. Something that only keeps a person's walk straight is a helper, not a shoe. The קב is made to carry the person's whole body weight, just like a shoe, so it gets the legal status of a shoe.

keyTerms.meaning: to lean on, to support one's weight
the wooden leg of an amputee

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words 'there it is made to straighten his walk' describe the OTHER item from the previous lines, not the wooden leg. The word הָכָא ('here') is what switches to the wooden leg.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of this passage. Because the קב is a real shoe, a woman may do חליצה with it. That is the basis of רבי יוחנן's correction below.

phrases.english: it is made to straighten his walk,
phrases.notes: Describes the other item, which only steadies the person.

phrases.english: here — it is made for leaning on,
and he actually leans on it.
phrases.notes: He puts his full weight on it, as one does with a shoe.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a contradiction raised on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on function (steadying versus weight-bearing)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both supports seemed alike, so they should share one law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a weight-bearing support counts as a shoe.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling on the chair-supports
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. The chair and supports of a disabled person can become טמא through מדרס, may not be worn out on שבת, and may not be brought into the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are susceptible to מדרס impurity. One may not go out with them on שבת, and one may not enter the עזרה with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a discussion about its exact wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These supports are used for leaning, so a זב who leans on them makes them טמא מדרס. Wearing them out on שבת is forbidden. The משנה also says they may not be brought into the Temple courtyard, and that last clause is about to be questioned.

keyTerms.meaning: susceptible to impurity from a זב's pressing weight
go out (into the public domain on שבת)

phrases.english: they are susceptible to impurity of treading,
and one may not go out with them on Shabbat,
and one may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.
phrases.notes: This clause is the focus of the next steps.

steps.triggerLanguage: טְמֵאִין מִדְרָס, וְאֵין יוֹצְאִין בָּהֶן בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Supports used for leaning are טמא מדרס, may not be worn out on שבת, and may not be brought into the עזרה.

steps.title: A reciter's opposite version of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: A תנא reciting before רבי יוחנן said the opposite: one MAY enter the עזרה with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: A reciter taught before רבי יוחנן: 'One may enter the עזרה with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: A reciter of משניות presents a different wording of the משנה. This sets up רבי יוחנן's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a תנא means a person who memorized and recited texts, not a sage of the משנה. His version permits bringing the supports into the עזרה, the direct opposite of our text.

keyTerms.meaning: a reciter who memorized משניות and ברייתות

steps.confusionAlert: This תנא is a professional reciter in the בית מדרש, not one of the תנאים of the משנה.

phrases.english: A reciter taught before Rabbi Yochanan:
'One may enter the Temple courtyard with them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a version that contradicts the wording quoted in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Alternate reading: the supports may be brought into the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן objects: it is a shoe
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן objects: he teaches that a woman may do חליצה with this support, so how can the reciter allow it into the עזרה?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I teach that a woman may do חליצה with it, and you say one may enter [the עזרה with it]?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges the reciter's version by pointing to his own ruling on חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חליצה is done with a shoe, so if this support works for חליצה, it is a real shoe. One may not enter the עזרה wearing shoes. The reciter's version therefore contradicts רבי יוחנן's teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: performs חליצה (removing the shoe of the brother-in-law)
the ceremony freeing a widow from יבום, done with a shoe

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows one ruling (shoe status for חליצה) controlling another area of law (entering the מקדש).

phrases.english: He said to him:
I teach 'a woman may perform chalitza with it,'
phrases.notes: This means it counts as a full shoe.

phrases.english: and you say 'one may enter'?!
phrases.notes: Shoes are not allowed in the עזרה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲנִי שׁוֹנֶה ״אִשָּׁה חוֹלֶצֶת בּוֹ״, וְאַתְּ אָמְרַתְּ ״נִכְנָסִין״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reading given in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reciter's version allowing entry into the עזרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Valid for חליצה means it is a shoe, and shoes are banned in the עזרה. So entry must be forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן corrects the text
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן tells the reciter to recite: 'One may NOT enter the עזרה with them.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Recite: 'One may not enter the עזרה with them.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן fixes the reciter's wording and confirms the version we have in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the support has the status of a shoe, the only consistent reading forbids bringing it into the עזרה. This matches the wording quoted in step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: A support that bears a person's full weight counts as a shoe. A woman may do חליצה with it, and it may not be brought into the עזרה.

phrases.english: Recite:
'One may not enter the Temple courtyard with them.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the corrected reading that follows from the objection in step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The correct reading is 'אֵין נִכְנָסִין בָּהֶן לָעֲזָרָה', because the support has the status of a shoe.

steps.title: What are לוקטמין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'לוקטמין are טהור' and asks what לוקטמין are.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'לוקטמין are טהור.' What are לוקטמין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes one more phrase from the משנה and asks what the unfamiliar word לוקטמין means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said the chair and supports of a disabled person are טמא through מדרס, but it said לוקטמין are טהור. To understand that contrast, we first need to know what object the word לוקטמין refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: An unclear object mentioned in the משנה; its meaning is debated below
What is it? (introduces a request for a definition)

phrases.english: Loketamin are pure.
What are loketamin?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the עזרה discussion ends, the גמרא returns to the next phrase in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definition of the word לוקטמין

steps.title: First definition: a toy donkey carried on the shoulders
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו says לוקטמין are a donkey carried on the shoulders.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is a 'donkey of the shoulders.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives the first answer. לוקטמין are a wooden toy donkey a person carries on his shoulders, so it looks as if the donkey is riding him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this view, לוקטמין is a toy for fun. It does not support the person's body the way a disabled person's chair or supports do.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
A donkey of the shoulder.
phrases.notes: A wooden toy shaped like a donkey, carried on the shoulders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לוקטמין are a toy donkey carried on the shoulders

steps.title: Second definition: stilts
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר פפא says לוקטמין are stilts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר פפא said: They are stilts.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר פפא gives a second, different answer: לוקטמין are stilts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stilts are used to walk above mud or just for fun. This is a different object from רבי אבהו's toy donkey, but the משנה's ruling that it is טהור stays the same.

phrases.english: Rava bar Pappa said:
Stilts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A competing answer to the same question

steps.title: Third definition: masks
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר רב הונא says לוקטמין are masks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר רב הונא said: They are masks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא בר רב הונא gives a third answer: לוקטמין are masks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we have three opinions about what the object is. The גמרא does not decide between them. All three agree with the משנה that לוקטמין are טהור.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three definitions of לוקטמין: a shoulder toy donkey (רבי אבהו), stilts (רבא בר פפא), and masks (רבא בר רב הונא).

phrases.english: Rava bar Rav Huna said:
Masks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third competing answer, which closes the definition discussion

steps.title: New משנה: boys with knots, princes with bells
steps.stepSummary: Boys may go out on שבת with קשרים, princes with bells, and in fact anyone may. The חכמים just described the usual case.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Boys may go out with knots, and princes with bells. And so may any person, but the חכמים spoke about what usually happens.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It permits boys to go out on שבת with healing knots and princes with bells, and adds that these rules really apply to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה names boys and princes only because they were the ones who usually wore these things. The phrase 'שדברו חכמים בהווה' tells us the ruling is not limited to them.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים spoke about the common, present case

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think only boys or only princes may wear these. The משנה itself says 'וכל אדם': everyone may. The examples are simply the usual situations.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
Young boys may go out with knots
and princes with bells,
and so may any person —
but the Sages spoke of the common case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה and a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone may go out on שבת with קשרים or bells. Boys and princes are mentioned only because they are the common case.

steps.title: What are the קשרים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the קשרים in the משנה are.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What are these knots?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the new משנה by asking what kind of knots the משנה means. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before we know why these knots are allowed on שבת, we need to know what they are. The answer will show they are a remedy, not just decoration.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What are knots?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of a word in the new משנה

steps.title: The knots are bundles of madder
steps.stepSummary: Through a chain of teachers, רב יהודה says the קשרים are bundles of פואה (madder).
steps.simpleTranslation: אדא מרי said in the name of רב נחמן בר ברוך, who said in the name of רב אשי בר אבין, who said in the name of רב יהודה: They are knotted bundles of madder.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers, passing down רב יהודה's teaching through a long chain of names: the knots are bundles of the madder plant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Madder was tied on for its healing power. Because the knots are a remedy the child wears, they count like clothing or jewelry, not like carrying.

keyTerms.meaning: Madder, a plant used for red dye and as a remedy

phrases.english: Adda Mari said
that Rav Naḥman bar Barukh said
that Rav Ashi bar Avin said
that Rav Yehuda said:
Bundles of madder.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַדָּא מָרִי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר בָּרוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קשרים are tied bundles of madder, worn as a remedy

steps.title: אביי's mother: how many madder bundles to use
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that three bundles hold an illness steady, five heal it, and seven work even against sorcery.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Mother told me: Three hold it in place, five heal, and seven work even against sorcery.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds practical advice from his foster mother about the madder bundles: the number of bundles changes how strong the remedy is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the definition in step 12. Three bundles stop the illness from getting worse, five cure it, and seven are strong enough even against witchcraft.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold in place, keeping the illness from spreading

steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's first explanation is that the קשרים are healing bundles of madder, and their number (3, 5, or 7) decides how strong the remedy is. The גמרא later rejects this as the meaning of the משנה (step 16) and replaces it in step 17.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Mother told me:
three keep it in place,
phrases.notes: They stop the illness from getting worse.

phrases.english: five heal,
seven are effective even against sorcery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds practical details about the madder remedy defined in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three madder bundles hold an illness steady, five heal it, and seven work even against sorcery.

steps.title: Conditions for the madder remedy to work
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says the פואה bundles only work if the patient avoids seeing sun, moon, and rain, and avoids hearing iron, a hen, and footsteps.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: The remedy only works if the person does not see the sun or moon, does not see rain, and does not hear the sound of iron, the sound of a hen, or the sound of footsteps.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב adds a set of conditions to אביי's statement about the healing power of the madder bundles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said the bundles hold back or heal an illness. רב אחא בר יעקב now limits this. The cure only works if the patient is cut off from certain sights and sounds. This makes the remedy much harder to use.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is only when; introduces a limiting condition

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:

phrases.aramaic: וְהוּא דְּלָא חֲזִי לֵיהּ שִׁמְשָׁא וְסֵיהֲרָא,
phrases.english: And that is only where he does not see the sun and the moon,
and does not see rain,
and does not hear the sound of iron,
or the sound of a hen, or the sound of footsteps.
phrases.notes: Sefaria translates תרנוגלא as 'hen'; it can also mean rooster.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: וְהוּא דְּלָא חֲזִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds limiting conditions to אביי's statement about the healing power of the bundles.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The madder remedy only works if the patient does not see sun, moon, or rain, and does not hear iron, a hen, or footsteps.

steps.title: The madder is like it fell into a pit
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק remarks that with so many conditions, the madder is useless.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: The madder fell into a pit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק reacts to the conditions of רב אחא בר יעקב with a sharp saying: the remedy is as good as lost.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No one can avoid all those sights and sounds in real life. So in practice the madder cure will never work. He is not arguing about the facts. He is pointing out that the conditions make the cure worthless.

keyTerms.meaning: Madder (the plant used in the bundles)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
The madder fell into a pit.
phrases.notes: An expression meaning: it is useless.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: נְפַל פּוּתָא בְּבֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the practical result of רב אחא בר יעקב's conditions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under such conditions, the madder remedy is practically useless.

steps.title: Why only young boys?
steps.stepSummary: If the קשרים are a healing remedy, the משנה should not have limited them to young boys. Girls and adults could use them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why specifically boys? Girls too! Why specifically young ones? Adults too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation that the קשרים are madder bundles. That explanation does not fit the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A medical cure helps anyone who is sick. Yet the משנה speaks only of 'young boys' (בנים קטנים). So the madder explanation leaves the משנה's specific wording unexplained.

keyTerms.meaning: Why specifically? (Why was this case singled out?)

steps.confusionAlert: This challenge is not against the healing power of madder itself. It only attacks the idea that madder is what the משנה meant by קשרים.

phrases.english: Why specifically boys?
Even girls too!
Why specifically young ones?
Even adults too!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא בָּנִים? אֲפִילּוּ בָּנוֹת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification of קשרים as madder bundles given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The identification of the משנה's קשרים as madder bundles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A medical remedy would apply to everyone. The משנה limits the קשרים to young boys, so the explanation does not match the משנה's wording.

steps.title: The קשרים are a strap for a boy who misses his father
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new explanation. The קשרים are a strap from the right shoe, tied on the left arm of a boy who longs for his father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what are the קשרים? Like what אבין בר הונא said in the name of רבי חמא בר גוריא: A son who longs for his father takes a strap from the right shoe and ties it on his left arm.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the madder explanation. It explains the קשרים as a special strap used for a child who misses his father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explanation fits the משנה's wording. Longing for a father is common in young children, and especially in boys. So the משנה naturally mentions 'young boys'. The challenge from the previous step is answered by changing what the קשרים are.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; signals a new explanation replacing the old one

steps.whatToRemember: The final explanation of the משנה's קשרים is a strap from the right shoe tied on the left arm of a young boy who misses his father. This explains why the משנה says 'young boys'.

phrases.english: Rather, what are the knots?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא
phrases.english: Like that which Avin bar Huna said
that Rabbi Chama bar Gurya said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּן שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּעְגּוּעִין עַל אָבִיו —
phrases.english: A son who has longings for his father,
one takes a strap from the right shoe
and ties it on his left arm.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַאי קְשָׁרִים — כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 by giving a new identification of the קשרים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition of the term in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The קשרים are madder bundles, a general medical remedy.
steps.terutzMaskana: The קשרים are a shoe-strap charm for young boys who long for their fathers. This fits the משנה's limitation to young boys.

steps.title: Memory aid: like תפילין
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק gives a memory aid. Tie it like תפילין: from the right onto the left. Doing the opposite is dangerous.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Your memory aid is תפילין. And the opposite is dangerous.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a simple way to remember which shoe and which arm to use.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תפילין are tied with the right hand onto the left arm. In the same way, the strap goes from the right shoe onto the left arm. Reversing it, from the left shoe onto the right arm, is dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Phylacteries, worn on the left arm and tied with the right hand

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
And your mnemonic is phylacteries,
and the opposite is dangerous.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: וְסִימָנָיךְ — תְּפִילִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a memory aid and a warning to the practice described in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tie it like תפילין: from the right shoe onto the left arm. Reversing it is dangerous.

steps.title: Placing an overturned cup on the navel on שבת
steps.stepSummary: In the name of the same teachers, the גמרא says it is permitted on שבת to put an overturned cup on the navel for healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבין בר הונא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא: Overturning a cup onto the navel on שבת is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a related topic. It brings another healing practice from the same teachers and rules that it is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous teaching came from אבין בר הונא in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא. So the גמרא now quotes another teaching from the same chain. A cup that held hot water is turned over onto the navel to ease pain. This is not considered forbidden healing on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it is permitted

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new series of teachings about which healing practices are allowed on שבת.

phrases.english: Avin bar Huna said
that Rav Chama bar Gurya said:
Overturning a cup onto the navel on Shabbat
is perfectly fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא: סַחוֹפֵי כָּסָא אַטִּיבּוּרֵי בְּשַׁבְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching from the same chain of teachers, moving to a new healing practice on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It is permitted on שבת to place an overturned cup on the navel for healing.

steps.title: Rubbing oil and salt on the body is permitted on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אבין בר הונא quotes רב חמא בר גוריא: one may rub oil and salt on oneself on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבין בר הונא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said: It is permitted to rub oil and salt on the body on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another ruling from the same pair of teachers. Rubbing oil and salt on the body is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling sits in the same series as the overturned cup on the navel in step 19. Each one is a body treatment that is still allowed on שבת. The next step will show what this oil-and-salt treatment was actually used for.

keyTerms.meaning: To rub or smear on the body

phrases.english: And Avin bar Huna said
Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said:
It is permitted to smear oil and salt on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another permitted body treatment to the list of rulings from the same teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing oil and salt on the body is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: How great rabbis were sobered up with oil and salt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the oil-and-salt practice in action. When רב הונא, רב, and רבי חייא left their teachers' houses drunk, oil and salt were rubbed on their palms and soles, along with a saying for sobering up. A backup method used a barrel's clay seal soaked in water.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what happened with רב הונא leaving the house of רב, רב leaving the house of רבי חייא, and רבי חייא leaving the house of רבי. When they were drunk, oil and salt would be brought and rubbed on their palms and the soles of their feet. Then someone would say: 'Just as this oil is clear, so may the wine of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, become clear.' And if not, he would bring the clay seal of a barrel, soak it in water, and say: 'Just as this clay seal is clear, so may the wine of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, become clear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the ruling from step 20 by showing when oil and salt were used: to sober up a drunk person. It also gives a second method in case the first is not available or does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 only said rubbing oil and salt is allowed. This story fills in the purpose: it helps a person who drank too much become clear-headed again. 'So-and-so, son of so-and-so' means the person's own name and his mother's name are said in the formula.

keyTerms.meaning: Palms of the hands and soles of the feet
The clay seal of a barrel
So-and-so, son of so-and-so (using the mother's name)

steps.confusionAlert: 'חַמְרֵיהּ' here means 'his wine,' as in the wine he drank. It does not mean 'his donkey' (חֲמָרָא). The formula asks for his wine to clear, meaning that he should become sober.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא מִבֵּי רַב,
phrases.english: As in this case of Rav Huna, leaving the house of Rav,
and Rav, leaving the house of Rabbi Ḥiyya,
and Rabbi Ḥiyya, leaving the house of Rabbi,
when they were drunk
they would bring oil and salt
and rub them on the palms of their hands
and the soles of their feet,
and say: 'Just as this oil is clear,
so may the wine of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, become clear.'
And if not, he would bring the clay seal of a barrel
and soak it in water,
and say: 'Just as this clay seal is clear,
so may the wine of so-and-so, son of so-and-so, become clear.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב הוּנָא מִבֵּי רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the real-life use of the oil-and-salt ruling from step 20.
steps.raayaObject: The oil-and-salt practice permitted in step 20. The story shows what the practice was used for (sobering up). It does not prove anything about שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice used for רב הונא, רב, and רבי חייא when they were drunk.

steps.title: Binding the neck to reset a dislocated vertebra is permitted
steps.stepSummary: The same teachers rule that one may tightly bind the neck on שבת to reset a dislocated vertebra.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבין בר הונא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said: It is permitted to 'choke' on שבת. This means tightly binding the neck of someone whose vertebra slipped out of place, in order to reset it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another ruling from the same pair. Tightly binding the neck as a medical treatment is allowed on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'לֵחָנֵק' sounds like choking, but here it means a tight neck bandage that pushes a slipped vertebra back into place. It is another treatment for the body that is permitted on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'to be choked.' Here it means to tightly bind the neck to reset a vertebra.

steps.confusionAlert: This ruling does not permit actual strangling. It refers to a tight medical binding of the neck.

phrases.english: And Avin bar Huna said
Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said:
It is permitted to strangle (tightly bind the neck) on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another treatment to the series of rulings from the same teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tightly binding the neck to reset a dislocated vertebra is permitted on שבת.

steps.title: Tightly swaddling a newborn is permitted on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The same teachers rule that one may tightly swaddle a baby on שבת so its limbs settle properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אבין בר הונא said that רב חמא בר גוריא said: Tightly swaddling a baby on שבת is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes this series with one more ruling. Wrapping a newborn tightly on שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A newborn's limbs may shift out of place during birth. Tight swaddling helps set them straight, so it counts as a treatment. Like the other rulings in this series, it is permitted on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: It is fine, it is permitted

steps.whatToRemember: אבין בר הונא, quoting רב חמא בר גוריא, lists several body treatments permitted on שבת: the overturned cup on the navel, rubbing oil and salt (used to sober up), tightly binding the neck, and tightly swaddling a newborn.

phrases.english: And Avin bar Huna said
Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said:
Swaddling a baby on Shabbat is well and permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אָבִין בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final ruling in the series from the same teachers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tightly swaddling a newborn on שבת is permitted.

steps.title: Two versions of the teaching about children
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רב פפא taught a version about 'children' (plural) and רב זביד taught a version about 'a child' (singular).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא taught 'children,' and רב זביד taught 'a child.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names two versions of the earlier rulings about children. This is a setup line, and the next step explains what each version means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of אבין בר הונא's rulings were about children: the shoe-strap knot for a boy who misses his father (step 17) and swaddling a baby (step 23). Here we learn that the students passed these down in two different ways. The words 'children' versus 'a child' stand for how many child-rulings each version credits to אבין בר הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: taught / passed down (a version of a teaching)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa taught 'children,'
Rav Zevid taught 'a child.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא מַתְנֵי ״בָּנִים״, רַב זְבִיד מַתְנֵי ״בֵּן״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the two rulings about children (the קשרים strap in step 17 and swaddling in step 23) and reports that they were transmitted in two versions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two versions: 'children' (רב פפא) and 'a child' (רב זביד).

steps.title: Explaining the two versions and who said the swaddling ruling
steps.stepSummary: In רב פפא's version, both rulings about children come from אבין בר הונא. In רב זביד's version, only the first ruling is his, and the swaddling ruling belongs to רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא taught 'children,' and he taught both rulings in the name of אבין בר הונא. רב זביד taught 'a child.' He taught the first ruling in the name of אבין בר הונא, and he taught this one in the name of רבה בר בר חנה. As רבה בר בר חנה said: swaddling a baby tightly on שבת is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the two versions from the last step. The only question is who said the swaddling ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree on the law itself: tightly swaddling a baby on שבת is allowed. They disagree only about who said it. 'Children' means two child-rulings credited to אבין בר הונא, while 'a child' means just one, because the swaddling ruling is really from רבה בר בר חנה.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody here disagrees about the law. Swaddling is allowed in both versions. The only argument is about which teacher said it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa taught 'children,'

phrases.aramaic: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מַתְנֵי לְהוּ בְּאָבִין בַּר הוּנָא.
phrases.english: and he taught both of them in the name of Avin bar Huna.
Rav Zevid taught 'a child':
the first one he taught in the name of Avin bar Huna,
phrases.notes: This means the earlier child ruling: the shoe-strap קשרים for a boy who longs for his father (step 17).

phrases.aramaic: וְהַאי מַתְנֵי לַהּ בְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה.
phrases.english: and this one he taught in the name of Rabba bar bar Ḥana.
As Rabba bar bar Ḥana said:
Tightly swaddling a baby on Shabbat
is fine.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ מַתְנֵי לְהוּ בְּאָבִין בַּר הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what each version in step 24 means.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Swaddling a baby on שבת is allowed. The versions differ only on whether אבין בר הונא or רבה בר בר חנה said it.

steps.title: Use the mother's name in incantations, and tie healing knots on the left
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports from the woman who raised him: incantations are said using the patient's mother's name, and healing knots are tied on the left side.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Mother told me, all repeated incantations are said with the name of the person's mother, and all healing knots are tied on the left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings rules about how remedies are done, which אביי learned from the woman who raised him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds practical details to the remedies the גמרא has been discussing. An incantation names the patient by their mother, and a healing knot is tied on the left side.

keyTerms.meaning: incantations that are repeated a set number of times

steps.confusionAlert: 'אֵם' here is not אביי's birth mother, who died when he was born. It is the woman who raised him.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Mother said to me:
All repeated incantations are said with the name of the mother,
and all knots are tied on the left.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new set of remedy rules from אביי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Incantations use the mother's name, and healing knots are tied on the left.

steps.title: How many times to say an incantation
steps.stepSummary: If an incantation comes with a set number of times, say it that many times. If not, say it 41 times.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: Mother told me, incantations with a stated number of times are said that many times, and those without a stated number are said forty-one times.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a second rule from the same woman, this time about how many times to say an incantation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule adds to the previous one. If the number of repetitions is given, follow it. If no number is given, the default is 41.

keyTerms.meaning: those that are spelled out (whose number is given)

phrases.english: And Abaye said: Mother said to me:
All incantations whose number is stated are said as stated,
and those not stated are said forty-one times.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second rule from the same source, also about incantations.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Say an incantation as many times as stated. If no number is stated, say it 41 times.

steps.title: Going out on שבת with a stone that prevents miscarriage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows a woman to go out on שבת wearing an אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה. רבי מאיר adds that even an object of the same weight is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: a woman may go out on שבת with an אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה. In the name of רבי מאיר they said: even with an object equal in weight to an אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that allows wearing a protective stone outside on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the stone is a recognized remedy, it counts like something worn, not a burden being carried. רבי מאיר holds that an object of equal weight works the same way, so it is allowed too.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'preservation stone' believed to prevent miscarriage

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the counterweight idea, which אביי limits in step 30 and questions in step 31.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may go out with a preservation stone on Shabbat.
In the name of Rabbi Meir they said:
Even with the counterweight of a preservation stone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יוֹצְאִין בְּאֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה בְּשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, protective objects worn on שבת, through a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה may be worn outside on שבת. According to רבי מאיר, so may an object of equal weight.

steps.title: The stone is allowed even before any miscarriage or pregnancy
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: this is allowed even for a woman who never miscarried, and even for one who is not yet pregnant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not only a woman who already miscarried, but even one who worries she might miscarry. Not only a woman who is pregnant, but even one who worries she might become pregnant and miscarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out which women may wear the stone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think the stone is only for a woman with a history of miscarriage, or one who is already pregnant. The ברייתא says no: it is allowed as a protection even for a future pregnancy, so the permission covers a very wide group.

phrases.english: And not only one who miscarried, but even lest she miscarry.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁעִיבְּרָה, אֶלָּא שֶׁמָּא תִּתְעַבֵּר וְתַפִּיל.
phrases.english: And not only one who is pregnant, but even lest she become pregnant and miscarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא by widening who may use the stone.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The stone may be worn as protection even with no past miscarriage and no current pregnancy.

steps.title: The counterweight must match by chance
steps.stepSummary: אביי (quoted by רב יימר בר שלמיא) says the counterweight works only if the object was found to match the stone's weight, not if it was changed to match.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא said in the name of אביי: this applies only when the object happened to be equal when he weighed it.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא adds a limit to רבי מאיר's counterweight rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The object must already weigh the same as the stone when it is weighed against it. If someone shaves or adds to an object until it matches, it does not count.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelamya said in the name of Abaye:
And this is when it came out equal when he weighed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי מאיר's counterweight rule from step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A counterweight works only if it naturally matched the stone's weight, not if it was adjusted to match.

steps.title: What about a counterweight of a counterweight?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks: does an object that matches the weight of the counterweight (not the stone itself) also work?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי asked: a counterweight of a counterweight, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks how far the counterweight idea goes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first counterweight works because it was weighed against the real stone. The question is whether this goes one more step: does an object weighed only against the counterweight also have the power?

phrases.english: Abaye asked:
A counterweight of a counterweight, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the counterweight rule one step further.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an object weighed against the counterweight (rather than the original stone) may also be worn on שבת.

steps.title: The question is left unresolved
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends with תיקו: the question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it stand (unresolved).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes אביי's question without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No source answers whether a second-level counterweight works, so the question stays open. Only the original stone and a first-level counterweight that matched by chance are clearly allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: let it stand: the question is left unresolved

steps.whatToRemember: An אֶבֶן תְּקוּמָה may be worn outside on שבת, even by a woman worried about a future pregnancy. According to רבי מאיר, an object of equal weight also works, but only if it matched without being adjusted. A counterweight of a counterweight is left as תיקו.

phrases.english: Let it stand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes אביי's question from step 31 without resolving it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether a counterweight of a counterweight works remains unresolved.

steps.title: First remedy for a one-day fever: salt weighed against a new coin
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports in his mother's name that for a one-day fever, one should weigh salt against a new white coin and tie it at the neckline with a thread of hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: And אביי said: My mother told me: For a fever that lasts one day, a person should take a new, shiny coin and go to the salt pools. There he should weigh out salt equal in weight to the coin. Then he should tie the salt at the opening of his collar with a thread made of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new remedy from אביי's mother, this time for a fever that lasts one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the series of remedies that אביי quotes from his mother. The cure has exact steps: a new coin, salt weighed to match it, and a specific place and thread for tying it.

keyTerms.meaning: A fever that lasts one day
Salt pools / a place where salt is made
The opening of the neckline (collar) of a garment

steps.whyThisMatters: The גמרא here records healing practices as accepted cures. This fits the wider sugya, which discusses healing objects and remedies and whether they may be used.

phrases.english: And Abaye said: Mother told me:
phrases.notes: אביי's 'mother' is the woman who raised him. She is quoted many times on this daf.

phrases.english: For a fever of one day,
let him take a white (new) coin,
and go to the salt pools,
and weigh its weight in salt,
and tie it at the opening of the neckline
phrases.notes: What gets tied is the salt.

phrases.english: with a thread of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the open question about the counterweight stone (Step 32) to a new remedy from אביי's mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For a one-day fever: weigh salt against a new coin and tie it at the neckline with a thread of hair.

steps.title: Second remedy: sealing a large ant in a copper tube
steps.stepSummary: If the salt remedy does not work, the person should catch a large ant carrying something, seal it in a copper tube, and say: 'Your burden on me, and my burden on you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, he should sit at a crossroads. When he sees a large ant carrying something, he should take it and put it in a copper tube. He should close the tube with lead and seal it with sixty seals. Then he should shake it, lift it, and say to it: 'Your burden is on me, and my burden is on you.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's mother gives a backup remedy, to be used if the first one fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is a swap: the ant is carrying a load, so the sick person takes the ant's load and gives the ant his fever. This exact wording, 'your burden on me', is what the next step will challenge.

phrases.english: And if not (if that did not work),
let him sit at a crossroads,
and when he sees a large ant
that is carrying something,
let him take it and put it in a copper tube,
and close it with lead,
and seal it with sixty seals,
and shake it, and lift it,
and say to it:
'Your burden is on me, and my burden is on you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A backup remedy in case the remedy of Step 33 fails.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Seal a burden-carrying ant in a copper tube and exchange burdens with it.

steps.title: Objection: someone may already have used this ant
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב הונא asks רב אשי: maybe another person already found this ant and gave it his own illness?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רב הונא, said to רב אשי: But maybe another person already found this ant and used it to end his own illness?
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא challenges the wording of the ant remedy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone else already gave this ant his sickness, then the ant's 'burden' is that person's illness. By saying 'your burden on me', the new user would take that stranger's illness onto himself.
steps.confusionAlert: רב אחא is not rejecting the remedy itself. He only objects to the words 'your burden on me', and the next step fixes them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Huna, said to Rav Ashi:
But perhaps a person (already) found it
and ended (his illness) with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the spoken formula given in Step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words 'טְעוּנָךְ עֲלַי' (your burden on me) in the ant remedy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ant already carries another person's illness, taking on its burden would bring that illness onto the speaker.

steps.title: Corrected wording: both burdens go on the ant
steps.stepSummary: Instead, one should say: 'My burden and your burden are on you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, he should say to it: 'My burden and your burden are on you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The wording of the ant remedy is fixed to answer the problem just raised.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new wording keeps the ant's burden on the ant and adds the speaker's fever to it. This way the speaker takes nothing back, so he cannot catch a stranger's illness.

phrases.english: Rather, let him say to it:
'My burden and your burden are on you.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection of Step 35 by changing the formula.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Say 'your burden on me and my burden on you' (an exchange).
steps.terutzMaskana: Say 'my burden and your burden are on you', so the speaker takes nothing back.
steps.whatToRemember: The ant remedy is kept, but with corrected words: everything goes onto the ant, and nothing comes back to the person.

steps.title: Third remedy: borrowing and returning river water
steps.stepSummary: If the ant remedy does not work, the person borrows a jug of water from a river, circles it around his head seven times, pours it out behind him, and returns it to the river.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if that does not work, he should take a new jug, go to the river, and say to it: 'River, river, lend me a jug of water for a guest who came to me.' Then he should circle the jug around his head seven times, pour the water out behind him, and say: 'River, river, take back the water you gave me. The guest who came to me came on its day and left on its day.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי's mother gives a third remedy, to be used if the second one fails.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fever is called a 'guest' that came for one day. The person borrows water 'for the guest' and then returns it, as a way of saying the guest has already left the same day it came.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי's mother gave three one-day-fever remedies in order: salt and a coin, then the ant, then the river water. Each one is a backup for the one before it.

phrases.english: And if not (if that did not work),
let him take a new jug,
and go to the river, and say to it:
'River, river, lend me a jug of water
for a guest who happened to come to me.'
And let him turn it around his head seven times,
and pour it out behind him, and say to it:
'River, river, take back the water that you gave me,
because the guest who happened to come to me
came on its day and left on its day.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list of backup remedies after the side discussion about wording in Steps 35-36.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Borrow a jug of river water 'for the guest', circle it around the head seven times, pour it out behind, and return it to the river.

steps.title: Introduction to a new statement of רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new statement by רב הונא. The statement itself continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is only a setup: the גמרא is introducing a new teaching from רב הונא, which comes in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. The words only tell us who is about to speak, and the content follows on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
phrases.notes: This attribution introduces a statement that continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the list of אביי's mother's remedies and opens a new speaker's teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only. רב הונא's statement continues on the next amud.
